Part 2 · TE-1 stage by stage

How does a finished case look?

Part 2 · the plan

One real run of TE-1, followed through

Open it yourself: Worked examples ▸ TE-1 ▸ Open example.

  1. Stage 0 to Definesymptom with numbers, the physics, the problem statement
  2. Explorefishbone, eight hypotheses, each with a falsifier
  3. Plan and Do itS/D/N screen, two tests, the fix and its check
  4. Look backthe barrier and the cost ledger

Stage 0 · the problem

“Reflux climbing, nothing obvious”

Situation given

The group runs TE-1 for 30 min of OTS time and touches nothing. Then it writes what was seen, by whom and when.

Stage 0 · trends · interactive

Thirty minutes on the DCS

Reflux and fuel climb with TIC-102 and TIC-101 on set point; the MPA temperatures move first.

Review R and Engage 1

Write the physics, then judge the urgency

\(Q = \dot m\, c_p\, \Delta T\)
  • MPA duty 3654 → 1936 kW: −47 %.
  • The tower must reject that heat at the top: more reflux.
  • Engage 1.4: keep running and investigate; no limit is near.

Define 2 · IS / IS NOT

Where the problem is, and where it is not

Explore 3.4 · cause and effect

Every idea on a bone first

Each bone idea becomes one working hypothesis on 3.6.

Explore 3.6 · working hypotheses

“If … then we should observe …”

  • Eight hypotheses, one per cause.
  • Each states what we should see and what would kill it.
  • A hypothesis without a falsifier cannot be tested.

Plan 4.3 · S / D / N · interactive

Screen the hypotheses with the evidence you already own

Evidence lines (tap to switch off)

One firm D drops a hypothesis; count the S only among the survivors.

Plan 4.6 · the plant-test plan

Two tests, written before anything is touched

Do it 5.0 · T-2 on the OTS · interactive

MPA flow +20 %: does the duty follow?

The duty rose only 11 % for 20 % more flow: E-4 itself limits the heat transfer. WH-7 killed; WH-1 confirmed.

Do it 5.5–5.6 · fix and verify

Clean E-4, then check against the prediction

  • 0:53:30: E-4 bundle cleaned and returned to service.
  • 45 min later: FIC-101 90.4 m³/h (design 89.5), TI-1014 209.9 °C (210.2).
  • Predicted before the fix: every line back to design.

Look back 6.4 · cost ledger · interactive

Was the troubleshooting worth it?

\(\text{fuel cost} = \Delta Q \cdot t \cdot \text{price},\ \Delta Q = 0.91\ \text{MW}\)

Prices are assumed teaching values, as in the workbook; the method is the point.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Numbers and times first; the MPA moved before the reflux.
  • Eight hypotheses, each with a falsifier; S/D/N left one.
  • One field round and one plant move proved it; the fix was checked.

Save · Report · Slides

The report writes itself from the record

  • Readiness check: all eight stages green.
  • Word report and team slides from the same record.
  • Save: .woods.json; File ▸ Open reloads it.

Rules for the graded cases

TE-1 is the model; TE-2 … TE-12 are yours

StepThe group does
Loadthe case in Exercises and the same case on Case & team
Run10–30 min of OTS time without touching anything
RecordPull all three; keep facts apart from opinions
Testwrite the plan, then make the one move
Hand in.woods.json, the report and the slides

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The readiness check shows what is still empty.
  • Report and slides come from the record, not from memory.
  • The .woods.json file is the hand-in.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Write the symptom with numbers, tags and times before any cause.

2

Give every hypothesis a falsifier you can read on the plant.

3

Screen with the evidence you own before you move anything.

4

Write the test plan first: one move, predictions, stop rule, way back.

5

Verify the fix against its prediction, then close the ledger.
